title: The Fish That Snipes Insects from Underwater 😱
script: This animal knocks prey out of the air — without jumping, without flying, with sniper-level accuracy. The archerfish fires a jet of water up to 3 meters, corrects for the way light bends between water and air, and almost never misses. But here's the wild part — it gets better by watching other archerfish shoot. Not instinct. Pure observation. Send this to someone who still thinks copying to learn is a human thing.
search_summary: Archerfish shoots water jets up to 3 meters to knock insects out of the air with sniper accuracy and learns by watching others.
comment_question: If a fish can learn by watching others, what's your excuse? 👀
